content: Keep some room in your heart for the unimaginable.
author: Mary Oliver
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. True art and creative work are not about clever technique; they demand total emotional skin in the game. When you create safely to please an audience or avoid criticism, the work feels hollow and bloodless.

Across his life and work, Mary Oliver saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Pouring your genuine spirit, vulnerability, and raw lived experience into what you make is what gives it enduring life. The work that resonates across centuries is always the work created with unapologetic personal truth.
reflectionPrompt: Take a conscious breath right now: how much of your current stress exists only in your anticipation of tomorrow?
